speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On behalf of all the Members in this House, I wish to thank you and your Deputies for presiding ably over the sessions and maintaining high standards for the proceedings.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our thanks also go to the Parliament Secretariat and support staff in the Chamber, in the Library, in the Members’ Room and at the Gate for their dedicated assistance, the translators who persevered along with us, as well as to all the officers from the Ministries and agencies who have worked hard to support us from behind the benches.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I wish also to extend my appreciation to the members of the media who have brought the debate to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Over the last eight days, Members in this House debated on what we can do, and how we can do better, to create a brighter future together.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These shifts present opportunities for growth, but also challenge the strength of our social compact.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As we embrace globalisation and technology to expand opportunities for our businesses, to transform industries and build deep capabilities, how do we ensure that we move forward together and leave no one behind?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Coupled with recent interest on the issue of social inequality, it comes as no surprise that the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) and Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) dominated much of the airtime in this Debate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members asked how we could support different segments of the workforce so that everyone has a place in the future economy, be it helping older workers and women, uplifting low-wage workers, or supporting freelancers and self-employed persons.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While we strive to transform our industries, Members were also concerned about the prospects of local firms, small and medium enterprises (SMEs), and displaced professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs), and how we can help them strengthen capabilities and remain competitive so that good jobs are created for our people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members' questions for MCCY reflect their interest in the softer aspects of nation-building.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members rightly highlighted that besides preparing our workforce for the future economy, we also need to strengthen social cohesion across race, religion and class lines, and create diverse and inclusive opportunities for Singaporeans to grow and pursue their aspirations.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Across the House, Members were concerned about whether Singapore was prepared to deal with external threats and internal challenges.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On foreign policy and security matters, Members debated how Singapore could respond to the changing geopolitical landscape, the dangers of segregationism and extremism, and the demands of cybersecurity.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I should remind the House of the role that you have played, Speaker, in planting the seeds of SG Cares.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: You have been a passionate advocate in calling upon Singaporeans to play an active part in creating a caring and cohesive society and you continue to co-chair the Committee with Desmond and I.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Indeed, nation-building goes beyond what the Government can do through its policies and efforts.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: So much more can be achieved when we do it as one united people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: With everyone playing their part, Singapore can stand fast in the face of challenges to come.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This speaks to the breadth and gravity of the issues we face today.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The debate over the past eight days has been vigorous.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: More importantly, Members of Parliament (MPs) stayed true to speaking up for their residents, for our people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: But beyond the figures and the measures we discussed, some Members searched deep – what are the purposes that we wish to achieve and how do we get there?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin reminded us that beyond being pragmatic in an uncertain future, we must also be bold enough to fight for our ideals.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: But I agree with Mr Murali Pillai that pragmatism and ideals are not mutually exclusive.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To tackle the problems of today and prepare ourselves for tomorrow, we must be bold and embrace change.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must have that grit and bias for action that make us an exceptional nation.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This would not be the case had we no ideals.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are an unexpected nation that triumphed against all odds.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through tenacity and sacrifice, through courage and adaptability, our forefathers built a nation that all of us can proudly call our Home.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They upheld the values and ideals of meritocracy, incorruptibility, multiracialism and personal responsibility to build a modern and vibrant city with opportunities for all.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Today, we can walk the streets feeling safe at night; we take clean air and water for granted; all our children go to good schools where guns and drugs are unheard of; and our youths have diverse opportunities to pursue their dreams.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singaporeans, young and old, are dreaming big and striving to give their best.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin observed that children in Singapore had big dreams, regardless of their socio-economic status.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We want to support them in achieving their ambitions.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is why I dedicated myself to public service.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: When I entered politics, I wanted to help build a Singapore where my children could grow up in a safe environment that protects them from harm, a Singapore where they can find meaningful work and opportunities to realise their potential, a Singapore where they can build a happy home and know the joy of raising their own families, and the space to find fulfilment and give back to society.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I believe this is a future that is shared by many of us here.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It is the legacy we wish to gift our children.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Government plays the role of an enabler.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Ultimately, success will depend less on what the Government does, but far more on what each and every one of us chooses to do today and every day.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To win the future, to ride out the challenges of income inequality, disruptive technology and an ageing society, we need the support of all Singaporeans, young and old, to nurture a strong society with an entrepreneurial dare and a smart nation with a heart.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Together with everyone in Singapore, we can build a strong Singapore society, anchored in meritocracy, self-reliance, hard work and compassion for the vulnerable and realise our ideal of being one united people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And where ideals and drive meet ability and opportunities, Singapore will be well-placed to seize the future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Some of you think that the biggest challenge being up here is how one manages to stay awake, or how we answer the calls of nature.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: What I find most challenging is having the desire to participate but not being able to do so in the way that all of you do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, what you all have is a unique precious privilege to make a significant impact on the well-being of our people.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I want to start by commending all of you for actively doing just that in the past few weeks.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Thanks also to my Clerks and Parliament colleagues who quietly help to keep the process running smoothly during this Budget and COS.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And on this topic of language, some of you have spoken of the importance.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing did raise some questions.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: A "set-top box" in Mandarin is "机 顶 盒" and analogue TV is "类 比 电 视".

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Of course, we remember Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat who, "spoiled market", oh, sorry, who raised the bar by speaking in Tamil not once, but twice.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So, the arms race has begun. "இது ஒரு பலமொழி நாடாளுமன்றம். என்னாலும் தமிழில் பேச முடியும்" This is a multi-lingual Parliament.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And of course, thank you so very much to all our Civil Servants and to our Leader and Whip.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: As I mentioned earlier, as Speaker, I do not speak, so I have no choice but to listen.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And there has been a lot of listening in these past few days!

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Rather than repeat what the Government has said, from this vantage point, allow me to try and see the wood for the trees.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I discern four core reasons from everything that you are saying.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is really about how we look after and make things better for Singaporeans as individuals, for Singapore, the community and society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And also, there is a time dimension of meeting today’s needs while catering for future ones.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There are tradeoffs and choices that need to be made, even when we focus on the very reasons for our existence.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is to discuss how we intend to realise our ideals, aspirations via plans and details.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The need to be pragmatic is as important as the ideals we hold dear.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Murali Pillai shared with us Joe Biden's quote, "Don’t tell me what you value, show me your budget, and I’d tell you what you value." Closer to home, in 1971, S Rajaratnam shared, "What you have done may not get as much publicity as utterances of professional oppositionists, but long after these have gone, what you have done will strengthen the democracy of deeds and not words." I know that in today's world, we sometimes like the smart sound bites, the eloquent emotive rhetoric.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But substance and details matter too, especially in the real Volatile, Uncertain, Complex and Ambiguous (VUCA) world, as Seah Kian Peng shared.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Difficult unpopular choices need sometimes to be made.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We all grapple with these dilemmas in our daily lives, as individuals, in our families, at school, at work, as leaders.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is no different at a national level.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But remember this, it is not about fear but how we thrive in this environment and embrace and seize the opportunities before us.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Thirdly, are we clear and united in where we are going?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: At times, things seem to be rather ambiguous, such as whether two-thirds plus one-third is greater than 1!

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Or disagreement, for example, having a division for the Budget Statement.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But when we look past the differences that are often amplified, do we not see that we have more points of convergence and agreement than not?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: These differences of opinions are important, and the debate helps us refine and clarify.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Argue, fight by all means, but within limits and in a responsible manner.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But I am thankful that, despite it all, we do have a unity of thought and conviction as to where we should go and how we should position ourselves as a nation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: So long as we do not hold ourselves back and be mired as others do, we can boldly more forward into the brave new world.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are laying the foundations for our future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We need to build a vibrant and innovative economy.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We intend to build a smart, green, liveable city.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Perhaps the question to ask is, who makes this happen?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: What will make us great as a nation and realise our vision will be when we are a people who will go the extra mile.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When we go the extra mile for one another because it is not just about me.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When we are able to look beyond self.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: This is about the heart and soul of our nation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Deep down inside all of us, I believe we know that these are fundamentally important, but, unlike everything else in the Budget, these cannot be mandated by law.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And it is for us, as Singaporeans, to respond.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I recently met a father of a chronically ill child at a Club Rainbow event.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: He shared that as a result of his child’s illness, he has learnt to be more patient, to be more loving and caring.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You see, change happens when we reach out and care for others.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: How else do we nurture this sense of looking beyond self?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: St Francis says that it is in giving that we receive.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And in the process, how we can perhaps begin to change.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And how we begin to become a better people, and a better society.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Whatever the future throws at us, we know we will fight for our survival and figure a way out.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: These are the qualities that will enable us to "pledge ourselves as one united people, so as to achieve happiness, prosperity and progress for our nation." So, I now take great pleasure in guillotining myself.
